'''''Linaria ricardoi''''' is a rare species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Plantaginaceae]] endemic to [[Portugal]].<ref name = "COL">{{cite web |url= http://www.catalogueoflife.org/DCA_Export/zip-fixed/2019-annual.zip|title= Species 2000 & ITIS Catalogue of Life: 2019 Annual Checklist.|author= Roskov Y. |year= 2019|publisher= Species 2000: Naturalis, Leiden, the Netherlands. ISSN 2405-884X. TaxonID: 53577402|accessdate= 2019-11-11}}</ref><ref name="source">{{cite web |title=World Plants: Synonymic Checklists of the Vascular Plants of the World |url=http://worldplants.webarchiv.kit.edu/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190318221109/http://worldplants.webarchiv.kit.edu/ |archive-date=2019-03-18 |access-date=2014-09-23 |last=Hassler |first=M. |date=2019 |publisher=Species 2000: Naturalis, Leiden, the Netherlands |issn=2405-884X}}</ref> Its scientific authority is Coutinho (Cout.).<ref name = "col53577402">Coutinho (1906) , In: Bot. Soc. Brot. 22: 131</ref> Locally known as ''"Linária dos Olivais"'' it blossoms from February to June.<ref name="icnf">{{Cite web |title=Plano Nacional de Conservação de Flora em Perigo |url=https://www.icnf.pt/api/file/doc/43b5c303be967109 |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=ICNF}}</ref>

== Description ==

An annual plant with linear and thick leaf with a slightly curled tip. The flowers (15-20) have a small violet corolla (9-12mm).<ref name="icnf" />

==Distribution and habitat==
''Linaria ricardoi'' is endemic to southern Portugal in the interior of [[Alentejo]] but the species' main distribution area is in the [[Beja District]] (specifically in [[Redondo, Portugal|Redondo]], [[Ferreira do Alentejo]], [[Beja, Portugal|Beja]], [[Alvito, Portugal|Alvito]], [[Cuba, Portugal|Cuba]] and [[Serpa]]). It is associated with grain fields such as [[wheat]] and [[oat]] and less commonly [[barley]], fallows and meadows in traditional or mounted [[olive]] groves, rarely on embankments and side roads. It thrives in these areas to the reduced application of herbidices.<ref name="icnf" /> It prefers clay and alkaline soils.<ref name="guia">{{Cite web |title=Guia da Flora de Portugal Continental Tomo I Parte 3|url=https://imprensanacional.pt/?w3n_livros_pdf=guia-da-flora-de-portugal-continental-tomo-i-parte-3 |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=Imprensa Nacional}}</ref>

==Threats==
It is threatened by agricultural intensification and the related increase in herbicide use starting in the 50s and intensified in the 70s. Its reduced distribution and population isolation make the species particularly vulnerable to natural and human threats. Overgrazing, botanical colectionism and droughts are other factors that can affect this plant.<ref name="iucn2011">{{cite iucn |author=Caldas, F.B. |date=2011 |title=''Linaria ricardoi'' |volume=2011 |article-number=e.T162017A5531306 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2011-1.RLTS.T162017A5531306.en |access-date=20 November 2021}}</ref><ref name="icnf" /> The conversion of tradional agriculture to intensive cultures in the region is a concerning issue, since 95% of its distribution coincides with the "Sistema Global de Rega do Alqueva", an expanding agricultural area created after the filling of the [[Alqueva Dam]].<ref name="alqueva">{{Cite web |title=Sistema Global de Rega do Alqueva |url=https://www.edia.pt/pt/o-que-e-o-alqueva/sistema-global-de-alqueva/ |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=EDIA}}</ref><ref name="flora" />

== Conservation ==
In 2006 [[Quercus (organization)|QUERCUS]] acquired a four hectare terrain with ''L. ricardoi'' habitat where repopulation accions were performed.<ref name="icnf" /><ref name="quercus">{{Cite web |title=Nova micro-reserva em Beja |url=https://quercus.pt/2021/03/nova-micro-reserva-biologica-na-regiao-de-beja/ |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=Quercus}}</ref><ref name="rtp">{{Cite web |title=Quercus cria micro-reserva na zona de Cuba para salvar planta endémica |url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/pais/quercus-cria-micro-reserva-na-zona-de-cuba-para-salvar-planta-endemica_n12574 |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=RTP}}</ref>
In 2011 it was considered to be a "Near Threatened" species by the IUCN but the "Lista Vermelha" update of 2020 classified it as "Endangered", due to the reduced EOO ({{cvt|2100|km2}}) and AOO ({{cvt|208|km2}}) in only 3 locations.<ref name="iucn2011" /><ref name="flora" /> A decreasing number of mature individuals, area of occupation and habitat quality led to an estimated population reduction over 30%. It is a protected species by portuguese law and the [[European Community]] through Annex II & IV of the [[Habitats Directive]], along with the Annex I of the [[Berne Convention on the Conservation of European Wildlife and Natural Habitats|Bern Convention]].<ref name=":Habitats">{{Cite web|url=https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:31992L0043&from=EN|title=Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora |website=Eur-Lex |access-date=29 January 2026}}</ref>

In 2022 it was selected as the portuguese "Plant of the Year" in order to raise awareness to its conservation.<ref name=":POY">{{Cite web|url=https://wilder.pt/historias/portugal-ja-escolheu-a-sua-planta-do-ano-2022 |title=Portugal já escolheu a sua planta do ano 2022 |website=Wilder |access-date=29 January 2026}}</ref>
